title: UNICEF's account of a hug, oxytocin, and cortisol
summary: UNICEF says that as a child gets older, a hug can help them regulate emotion, because a hug releases oxytocin and calms the release of cortisol.
body: UNICEF Parenting says cuddling and skin-to-skin contact comfort a baby, who is described as being comforted by the caregiver's heartbeat and as getting to know the caregiver's smell. For a somewhat older child, the page says hugging can help them learn to regulate emotions and manage stress. The reason it gives is that a hug leads the brain to release oxytocin and calms the release of cortisol. That chemical sentence is UNICEF's explanation for families. A laboratory paper measuring those chemicals was not opened for this card.
